newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hansol sees '96 net at 1995 level of 40.3 bln won.
newsitem.headline: Hansol sees '96 net at 1995 level of 40.3 bln won.

text.p: South Korea's Hansol Paper Co Ltd said on Monday that its 1996 net profit was expected to be around the 1995 level of 40.3 billion won, while turnover was seen rising to over one trillion won in 1996 from 887.8 billion a year ago.
"High pulp prices has been squeezing profits this year," said Hansol spokesman Lee Jin-kyu.
But the firm's sales were boosted by capacity expansion in printing paper production, he added.
Hansol, the nation's largest paper manufacturer, is expected to become the first paper maker in South Korea to post an annual turnover over one trillion won, Lee said.
